question: The depositional pattern of CaCO₃ and other materials that extend upwards from the floor of a limestone cavern is known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Stalagmite**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **stalagmite** is a type of rock formation that rises from the floor of a cave due to the accumulation of material deposited on the floor from ceiling drippings.
 
• These formations are typically composed of **calcium carbonate (CaCO3)** and other minerals.
 
• Stalagmites grow upwards from the floor, as opposed to **stalactites**, which hang from the ceiling of caves.
 
• The growth of stalagmites is influenced by the rate of dripping water and the concentration of minerals in the water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stalactites** and stalagmites are often found in pairs, with stalactites hanging from the ceiling and stalagmites growing from the ground directly below them.
 
• When a stalactite and stalagmite meet, they form a column or pillar.
 
• The formation of these structures can take thousands of years, depending on the environmental conditions within the cave.
 
• Both formations are key attractions in many limestone caves around the world, drawing interest from tourists and geologists alike.
